2. Cod. f. 229 a. XXXII. 6. Καὶ τοῦτο ἐν τοῖς μάλιστα τὴν ἀλληγορίαν δείκνυσι τῆς Γραφῆς· ὁ γοῦν Φαραὼ σωματικῶς οὐκ ἂν ἀπὸ τῶν προχωρημάτω αὐτοῦ ποτίσαι τὴν γῆν, ἀλλʼ ἡ σκυβαλώδης ἔκκρισις τοῦ ἀντικειμένου ποτίζει τὰ γήϊνα.
3. Cod. f. 222 b. XXXII. 23. Ὁ Ἑβραῖος ἐν μήκει λάκκου ἔχει· τὸ γὰρ ἰαρὴχ κατὰ τὴν Ἐβραίων φωνὴν δασέως προφερόμενον, καὶ μηρὸν, καὶ μῆκος σημαίνει· τὸ δὲ αὐτῆς πρὸς τὴν συναγωγὴν ἔχει τὴν ἐπίδοσιν· λάκκον οὖν καλεῖ τῆς ταφῆς τὸ βάθος· μῆκος δὲ, τῆς ταφῆς τὴν ἔκτασιν.
thought_title: Allegory of Pharaoh's watering and the Hebrew word for pit and length
orientation: Origen is commenting on Ezekiel 32, explaining that Pharaoh's watering of the land must be read allegorically, and then discussing the Hebrew word behind 'pit' in Ezekiel 32:23.
pass_a_gloss: And this especially shows the allegory of Scripture; Pharaoh, at any rate, would not bodily water the earth from his excrements, but the filthy discharge of the adversary waters earthly things. The Hebrew has 'in the length of the pit'; for the word iarech, pronounced with aspiration according to the speech of the Hebrews, signifies both thigh and length; and it has its application to the gathering; therefore he calls the depth of burial a pit; and length, the extent of burial.

choices.why: προχώρημα means excrement, confirmed by the parallel σκυβαλώδης ἔκκρισις in the next clause
matches the glossary term for the foul discharge of the adversary
standard Origen term for the devil, consistent with the brief's cast
neuter plural substantive, preserving the allegorical contrast with heavenly things

choices.term: λάκκον οὖν καλεῖ τῆς ταφῆς τὸ βάθος
choices.english: therefore he calls the depth of burial a pit
choices.why: preserves the word order and the identification of pit with depth of burial
rejected: he calls the pit the depth of burial

choices.term: μῆκος δὲ, τῆς ταφῆς τὴν ἔκτασιν
choices.english: and length, the extent of burial
choices.why: preserves the parallel structure: length is identified with the extent of burial
rejected: and length means the extent of burial

bible_refs.note: Ὁ Ἑβραῖος ἐν μήκει λάκκου ἔχει

pass_b_english: This above all shows the allegory of Scripture: Pharaoh would not literally water the earth from his excrements, but the filthy discharge of the adversary waters earthly things.

The Hebrew has “in the length of the pit.” For the word iarech, pronounced with aspiration in the Hebrew tongue, means both “thigh” and “length.” The pit, therefore, he calls the depth of burial, and length the extent of burial.
